study.title: Altered periaqueductal gray resting state functional connectivity in migraine and the modulation effect of treatment
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial with resting-state fMRI; patients randomized to verum acupuncture, sham acupuncture, and waiting list groups; healthy controls recruited for baseline comparison
study.randomization: All MwoA patients were randomized into five groups
study.population: Migraine without aura (MwoA) patients and age- and sex-matched healthy controls, aged 17–45 years, right-handed
study.inclusion_criteria: MwoA patients: (1) aged between 17–45 years and right-handed, (2) had not taken any prophylactic headache medicine, or acupuncture treatment during the last three months, (3) had at least six months of migraine duration, and (4) had at least one headache attack per month during the last three months. Healthy controls: right-handed, aged between 17–45 years, free from any chronic pain conditions
study.exclusion_criteria: Patients excluded if they: (1) were alcohol or drug abusers, (2) were pregnant or during lactation, (3) suffered from psychiatric, neurologic, cardiovascular, respiratory or renal illnesses, (4) suffered from any other chronic pain conditions or had a history of head trauma, with loss of consciousness, (5) had MRI contraindications, such as claustrophobia, and (6) had acupuncture contraindications, such as bleeding tendency. HC excluded if: abnormal test results or a history of head trauma with loss of consciousness, pregnancy or lactation

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: BOLD resting-state functional images obtained with echo-planar imaging; structural: three-dimensional MRI sequence employing an axial fast spoiled gradient recalled sequence
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: functional: 30 contiguous slices with a slice thickness of 5mm; field of view, 240×240mm2; data matrix, 64×64; re-sampled to 3-mm cubic voxels; structural: voxel size of 1 mm3, data matrix 256×256, field of view 256×256mm2
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: DPARSFA (Data Processing Assistant for Resting State fMRI, Advanced) based on SPM8
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: normalized by using structural image unified segmentation
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: smoothed with a 6 mm full-width half-maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Subjects with head movements exceeding 2 mm on any axis or head rotation greater than 2° were excluded. Scrubbing: removed frames with FD >0.5mm, one time point before 'bad' time points and two time points after 'bad' time points were deleted
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: regressed out 6 head motion parameters, white matter signal and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) signal
statistical_thresholds_exact: voxel-wise P< 0.005 uncorrected and P< 0.05 family wise error (FWE) correction at cluster level
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: P< 0.05 family wise error (FWE) correction at cluster level

extraction_notes.note: The arm 'AG' (acupuncture group, verum + sham merged) is not a separate randomization unit but a post-hoc merged group created by the authors for analyses. Its arm_id is flagged accordingly. n_analyzed_neuroimaging for AG = 46 (n=11 VA1 + n=11 VA2 + n=13 VA3 + n=11 SA).

For contrast C01 (HC > MwoA), the table lists two cluster entries (voxels 297 and 196) with multiple peaks each. It is unclear whether mPFC and rACC rows (C01_R2, C01_R3, C01_R4) belong to the 297-voxel cluster or are separate sub-peaks within it. Based on table formatting, they appear to be sub-peaks of the 297-voxel cluster. Cluster size 196 is assigned to the second L OFC entry only.

For contrast C04 (Post > Pre in AG), the table shows a single cluster of 408 voxels with multiple peaks across L MCC, L mPFC, L rACC, R MCC, R rACC. These sub-peaks are all listed under the same cluster size (408).
For contrast C05 (AG > WT), the table shows a single cluster of 501 voxels with multiple peaks across L MCC, L mPFC, L rACC, R rACC. These sub-peaks are all listed under the same cluster size (501).

For contrast C07 (negative association between VAS change and rs-fc change in AG), multiple sub-clusters appear: 523 voxels for MCC/rACC/frontal regions, 296 voxels for putamen/caudate/thalamus, 300 voxels for cerebellum. These appear to be separate clusters based on Table 5 formatting.

Sample sizes for the neuroimaging analyses are not always clearly stated per contrast. n=104 is inferred for baseline group comparisons (HC n=42 + MwoA patients at baseline n=62 who completed two MRI scans). The text states 88 patients participated in the first fMRI scan, but Table 1 and the flow chart indicate 62 patients completed both scans with complete MRI data.
No expectancy, credibility, or blinding success data were reported. The paper does not appear to have assessed these constructs formally.
No adverse events data were reported in this paper.

Deqi was described qualitatively but not quantitatively measured (no MASS or other validated deqi scale scores reported). The paper acknowledges this as a limitation: 'We did not quantitatively record intensity of deqi sensation'.
The paper does not report blinding assessment or participant/assessor guessing of allocation.

Coordinate space is not stated explicitly in the paper, but the use of MNI normalization via SPM8 unified segmentation strongly implies MNI space. This is reflected in the coordinate_space_reported_exact field as 'MNI'.
For contrast C08 (verum > sham), the n_analyzed is not explicitly stated for the sham vs verum sub-comparison. VA1+VA2+VA3 = 33 verum; SA = 11 sham at the neuroimaging analysis level.

The paper states that the 3 verum acupuncture groups (VA1, VA2, VA3) differed by acupoints used, but the needle type, depth, retention, and manipulation procedures were identical across groups. The sham group used the same physical procedure (penetrating needle, deqi intended) at non-acupoints, making it a 'non-acupoint sham' design rather than a non-penetrating sham.

The paper uses the label 'v1PAG' in results text and table but this appears to be a typographical variant of 'vlPAG' (ventrolateral periaqueductal gray). All such references have been treated as vlPAG.

Table 4 column for 'Changes of vlPAG resting state-functional connectivity in MwoA patients due to acupuncture treatment (verum+sham): Pre>Post' states 'No brain region above the threshold', consistent with the text. This has been noted but not separately tabulated as a zero-result contrast entry.

The 'n_total_analyzed_neuroimaging' of 104 reflects the 42 HC plus 62 MwoA patients who completed both MRI scans with complete data, as this is the combined sample used for the HC vs MwoA baseline comparison. The 46 MwoA patients in the AG were used for pre-post neuroimaging comparisons.
